subject: DPA roles, SCCs and transfer addendum — timeline & redline next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@crescenthealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@crescenthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA roles & SCCs — execution timeline and Qs

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the MSA/order form and we have a few open items in the DPA that we need clarified before procurement can issue a PO:

- Which role mapping are you proposing on the order form? Crescent is expecting controller-controller for some datasets; your standard draft labels Redwood as processor. Can you confirm if controller-controller is an option and what the implications are?
- We need the SCCs template you intend to attach and confirmation whether you will sign a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) for EEA->US flows.
- KMS/encryption: do you offer a bring-your-own-key option for Dedicated or Private deployments? If not, what are the contractual commitments around key management?

I attached our DPA draft (Crescent_DPA_draft_v1.docx) with comments in the margins. Procurement is on a tight timeline — can you share a redline and an expected sign-off ETA?

Also copying Elena (legal) to keep the loop.

Best,
Samir
Head of Procurement
Crescent Health

--- Attachment: Crescent_DPA_draft_v1.docx (docx, 140KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA roles & SCCs — execution timeline and Qs

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear notes and the draft.

Short answers up front:
- Role mapping: our default is Processor for hosted/Redwood-managed models. We can consider Controller-Controller for limited data classes if Crescent requires (this usually triggers additional operational controls and a commercial addendum).
- SCCs/TIA: we use the EU Commission SCCs (2021) and can append a transfer impact addendum in cases where controller-controller is requested.
- KMS: BYOK is available on Private deployments; for Hosted we provide managed keys with encryption at rest and in transit and can discuss KMS integration on Dedicated.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached our initial redline to your draft (Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.docx) with the team’s high-level positions.
2) Can Crescent confirm required hosting regions and whether controller-controller is non-negotiable for all PII?
3) If controller-controller is required, we will route to legal for a scoped addendum. Laura — can you review the attached redline and flag anything that needs exec clearance?

Proposed ETA: internal legal review today; call with Crescent legal by EOD tomorrow if that works (30 min). HubSpot: HS-3321 (linked).

Thanks — Naomi
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.inference.com

Looping in sales context — DL-7782.

Samir, to add a commercial note: if Crescent requires controller-controller or BYOK on hosted traffic, that typically moves the deal to Dedicated/Private, which will affect pricing and lead time. If timeline is tight and processor role is acceptable for non-regulated datasets, we can keep to hosted and accelerate signature.

Action items for us:
- Confirm hosting regions (NA-only vs EU/NA).
- Get Crescent legal on a 30-min redline call tomorrow (Naomi to schedule).
- Hold provisional PO timeline: procurement indicated they need signed docs within 10 business days.

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@crescenthealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA roles & SCCs — execution timeline and Qs

Samir / Naomi — I reviewed the Crescent draft and Naomi’s redline. High level positions and suggested language below (I’ve attached a formal PDF redline):

1) Role mapping
- Proposal: Default position remains Processor unless Crescent provides a narrow list of data categories requiring controller-controller (e.g., patient identifiers used for direct care). If Crescent confirms those categories, we will accept controller-controller for those categories only and insert a carveout in Section 2.2.

2) SCCs & TIA
- We will append the 2021 SCCs. Where controller-controller is accepted, Redwood will sign a Transfer Impact Addendum limited to the agreed data categories. Please confirm required safeguards and whether Crescent needs the full technical assessment (we can provide an executive summary).

3) Subprocessors & KMS
- Subprocessor disclosure schedule: we will provide current subprocessors; contract will include a 30-day notice for changes.
- BYOK: available for Private deployments. For Dedicated we can evaluate a KMS integration with commercial terms; for Hosted we will provide managed keys and SOC 2 evidence.

4) Evidence & timing
- Please provide Crescent’s procurement evidence list (SOC 2 Type II, DPIA summary if applicable). We can turn around a legal redline + internal approval recommendation within 2 business days once hosting scope is confirmed.

If Crescent can scope hosting to NA-only and limit controller-controller to a named data class, I can greenlight the redline without exec escalation. Otherwise, per Ben, we’ll need commercial sign-off (possible pricing concession).

Next: Naomi — please schedule the redline call tomorrow morning; Samir / Elena — confirm hosting region and the specific data categories that Crescent considers controller-controller.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: Legal_Redlines_v1.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference.com>

Thanks team — quick decision lane:

- If Crescent confirms NA-only hosting and narrows controller-controller to a named data class, Legal may proceed with the redline we discussed and I approve.
- If Crescent requires cross-border controller-controller for broad PII classes, we escalate to SVP Sales for commercial concession (possible uplift or implementation SOW).

Operational impact: controller-controller + cross-border requires playbooking with Infra (30-45 day lead on Dedicated provisioning in typical cases). Sales, please surface the expected PO date so we can prioritize capacity.

Jonas Weber
VP, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
